rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.4-2.6 and 3 (Tables 1, 3, 4, 5; Figs 4-10) - the authors process nine Landsat scenes (1987, 2000, 2014) with NDWI and one Sentinel-2 scene (2024) with SVM to compute surface water areas of Therthar, Razzazah and Haditha lakes themselves.
rows.notes: The study's own result is the mapping of surface-water area change in three Iraqi lakes (e.g., Razzazah -67% 2000-2014, Therthar -28% and Haditha -12.6% 1987-2014, further shrinkage in 2024) and a description of shape changes. This supports only the first half of the passage (spatial tracking of declining water coverage). The claimed function (support for early warning systems and regional water allocation strategies) is not tested or demonstrated: the authors only recommend in the Conclusions that the technique 'can be exploited' for periodic monthly/quarterly checks and state the work 'provides methodological guidelines' for water management. No early-warning or allocation application is implemented or evaluated, so the study is upstream of the claimed effect. No accuracy assessment, ground validation, dispersion measure or triangulation of the area estimates is reported; the only limitations stated (Section 2.4) concern the Landsat data (small water bodies, 16-day revisit, cloud cover, ETM+ SLC-off), not the claimed risk-management effect.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a descriptive remote-sensing change-detection paper on lake surface area; drivers of decline are discussed as possibilities with literature citations rather than analysed with own data.
